title: Under-Sink Kitchen Rack: Maximize Hidden Space Below Your Sink (2026)
excerpt: Complete guide to choosing and installing under-sink kitchen racks. Tips for maximizing space, organizer types, waterproofing, and top product recommendations for 2026.
content: An under-sink kitchen rack is a smart solution to maximize the hidden space below your sink that often gets cluttered. With the **right under-sink rack**, the area beneath your sink can transform from a dumping ground into an organized, functional storage space.
From our perspective shipping daily to homes across Indonesia, smaller spaces often end up more organized because their owners are more disciplined.
![Neatly organized under-sink kitchen rack below a modern kitchen sink](/images/blog/rak-kolong-dapur-hero.webp)

Most Indonesian households only use 30-40% of the storage capacity under their kitchen sink. The rest is wasted because of the irregular shape of the area and pipes blocking the space. This article will help you overcome these challenges with a complete guide to choosing, installing, and optimizing your under-sink kitchen rack.

> **Key Takeaways:**
> - Choose products with clear safety labels (food-grade, BPA-free) for daily use
> - Investing slightly more in quality materials (glass, grade 304 stainless steel) saves long-term costs
> - Match sizes to family needs, neither too large nor too small
> - Local marketplaces like Tokopedia, Shopee, and [Sesoris](https://www.sesoris.com/) offer competitive prices with maintained quality
## Why Is the Under-Sink Area Often Neglected?

The space under the sink has unique challenges that make it difficult to manage. First, there are water drainage pipes that cut through the space vertically. Second, the area isn't perfectly square-shaped because it follows the kitchen cabinet construction. Third, there's a moisture risk from pipes that could damage items. For additional information, also see the guide from [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com/).

However, because of these challenges, under-sink racks are specially designed with features that address all these issues. Modern racks have modular designs that can be adjusted to accommodate pipes, water-resistant materials, and adequate air ventilation.
If you're reorganizing your entire kitchen, our guide on [organizing a small kitchen effectively](/blog/mengorganisir-dapur-kecil-dengan-efektif) could be an additional reference that's very useful.
## Types of Under-Sink Kitchen Racks
### 1. Expandable Tier Shelf

This rack has an adjustable width (expandable) to fit your cabinet size. It typically consists of 2 tiers with a U or V shape in the back to avoid pipes. This is the most popular type because of its flexibility. For additional information, also see the guide from [Real Simple](https://www.realsimple.com/).
### 2. Pull-Out Drawer
A pull-out drawer system installed inside the lower cabinet. You simply pull the drawer out to access items in the back without bending down or reaching deep. More expensive but much more ergonomic.
### 3. Lazy Susan Under Sink
A round rack that rotates 360 degrees, commonly used for storing cleaning bottles and soap. Makes it easy to access all items without moving other things around.
### 4. Cabinet Door Hanging Rack
A rack attached to the inside of the cabinet door. Very efficient because it uses space that's usually empty. Great for storing sponges, rubber gloves, plastic bags, and other lightweight items.
### 5. Modular Box Organizer
A system of plastic boxes that can be stacked and configured as needed. Very flexible since each module can be moved to different positions. Perfect for non-standard shaped cabinets.

## What Should You Store Under the Sink?
Not all items are suitable for storage under the sink. Here's a guide to ideal items and what to avoid:
### Suitable Items
- Dish soap and detergent
- Floor cleaner and multi-purpose cleaners
- Sponges, brushes, and cleaning tools
- Garbage bags and plastic bags
- Rubber gloves
- Small organic waste container
### Items to Avoid
- Food - risk of contamination from cleaning chemicals
- Electrical appliances - moisture hazard
- Documents or paper - easily damaged by humidity
- Medications - unstable temperature and humidity

## Under-Sink Kitchen Rack Installation Guide
Installing an under-sink kitchen rack doesn't require special skills. Follow these steps for optimal results:
1. **Empty the cabinet** - remove all items and clean the area of dust and dirt
2. **Measure cabinet dimensions** - note the width, depth, height, and pipe positions
3. **Check pipe condition** - make sure there are no leaks before installing the rack
4. **Install water protection** - place a silicone mat or plastic liner on the cabinet floor
5. **Assemble the rack per instructions** - for expandable racks, adjust the width to fit your cabinet
6. **Position rack to avoid pipes** - use the U or V opening on the rack to accommodate pipes
7. **Test stability** - make sure the rack doesn't wobble before placing items on it
8. **Organize items by category** - group similar items and place frequently used ones in front
## Under-Sink Waterproofing Tips
Moisture is the main enemy of the under-sink area. Here are effective waterproofing strategies:
- **Install a drip tray** - place a shallow pan under pipe joints to catch water drips
- **Use waterproof shelf liner** - line the cabinet floor with EVA or silicone material
- **Install a leak detector** - a simple water sensor that alerts you when it detects pooling water
- **Ensure adequate ventilation** - don't pack items too tightly so air can circulate
- **Inspect regularly** - check pipe conditions and joints at least monthly

For extra protection, consider using waterproof storage containers. A complete review of container options can be found in our [review of Sesoris's versatile container collection](/blog/review-koleksi-kontainer-serbaguna-sesoris).

## How to Maximize Under-Sink Space
Here are tricks used by professional organizers to maximize every inch of your under-sink area:
### Utilize Vertical Space

Most people only use the cabinet floor space. But the vertical space above items can still be used with tier racks or hanging solutions. Install a tension rod at the top of the cabinet to hang spray bottles.
### Use the Cabinet Door
The inside of the lower cabinet door is valuable real estate that's often forgotten. Install a door organizer to store sponges, gloves, recipes, or shopping lists.
### Group Items in Labeled Containers
Use clear plastic containers with labels - one for kitchen cleaning tools, one for floor cleaner, one for soap backup. This system makes searching easier and keeps things tidy.
### Consider Lazy Susan for Corners
For L-shaped corner cabinets, a lazy susan is a lifesaver. You can access all items by rotating the platform without reaching into the far corner.

## FAQ About Under-Sink Kitchen Racks
### Can under-sink racks be installed on all kitchen cabinet types?

Yes, most under-sink racks are designed to be compatible with various kitchen cabinet types. Expandable racks can be adjusted from 38 to 70 cm wide, covering standard Indonesian cabinet sizes. For custom kitchen sets with non-standard sizes, choose modular box types that are more flexible to configure.
### How do you deal with bad smells under the sink?

Bad odors under the sink are usually caused by standing water or small leaks in the pipes. First, check and fix any leaks. Second, place open baking soda in a container to absorb odors. Third, ensure adequate ventilation by not filling the space too full. Fourth, clean this area at least every two weeks.
### What material makes the most durable under-sink rack?

For the damp under-sink area, powder-coated steel and food-grade PP plastic are the most durable choices. Powder-coated steel is rust-resistant and strong, while PP plastic is unaffected by moisture. Avoid racks made from uncoated steel or MDF wood that are easily damaged by water.
### What is the typical maximum load capacity of under-sink racks?

Maximum load capacity varies depending on type and material. Steel expandable racks typically hold 8-15 kg per tier. Quality pull-out drawers can hold 15-25 kg. Door-hanging racks usually only hold 3-5 kg. Always check the manufacturer's maximum load specifications and don't exceed the stated limits.
### Do you need to hire a professional to install an under-sink rack?

For most under-sink rack types, you can install them yourself without professional help. Expandable racks, modular boxes, and door organizers just need assembly and placement. Pull-out drawers might need professional installation since they require permanent mounting with screws inside the cabinet, especially if you're not comfortable using a drill.
**Q: How long do quality home organization products typically last?**

With proper routine care, food-grade plastic products last 3-5 years, while borosilicate glass and grade 304 stainless steel can last 10+ years. Key factors are consistent maintenance and avoiding extreme temperature exposure.
**Q: Is this product food-safe?**

Ensure the product is labeled "food-grade" or "BPA-free" before using it for food storage. Safe materials include borosilicate glass, grade 304 stainless steel, and certified food-grade plastic. Avoid plastic without food safety certification, especially for hot or oily foods.
**Q: How do I clean and maintain it?**

Wash with mild dish soap and warm water. Avoid abrasive sponges that can scratch the surface. For stubborn stains, use a baking soda and water paste as a natural cleaner. Dry completely before storing to prevent mold and bacteria.
**Q: What is the price difference between local and imported products?**

Local Indonesian products are typically 30-50% more affordable than imports of similar quality. For daily home organization needs, local products meet the standard. Consider imports only if you need specific features not available in the local market.
